borrower.naicsDescription: Farm and Garden Machinery and Equipment Wholesalers

tailwinds: Texas Hill Country housing growth at 4.2% annually drives outdoor equipment demand
headwinds: Tariff exposure on imported small engines (Honda, Stihl, Briggs & Stratton)

risks.title: Customer Concentration
risks.finding: Top 3 customers account for 31% of revenue
risks.source: Customer ledger report, 2024 fiscal year, page 4
risks.mitigant: All three are 7+ year relationships with recurring service contracts. No customer has signaled intent to leave.

risks.title: Tariff Exposure on Imported Inventory
risks.finding: 62% of inventory consists of imported small engines subject to current US tariff schedules
risks.mitigant: Pricing power demonstrated in the 2023 tariff round, with full pass-through to customers and stable gross margins

risks.title: Collateral Coverage Tight
risks.finding: Total advance value is 1.01x the loan amount
risks.source: Real estate appraisal plus equipment and inventory schedules
risks.mitigant: SBA 75% guaranty plus owner personal guarantee backed by $890K net worth

scenarios.label: Rates rise 200bps
scenarios.memoOverride: Approve with original conditions. DSCR remains well above the 1.25x bank floor under a 200bps rate shock.
scenarios.avatarScript: DSCR drops to 2.13x. Still very strong. No covenant changes needed. The deal holds up well under rate pressure.

scenarios.label: Top customer leaves
scenarios.memoOverride: Approve with stricter conditions: quarterly DSCR test instead of annual, and customer concentration review at every renewal.
scenarios.avatarScript: DSCR drops to 1.83x. Still bankable, but I'm tightening the covenants. I want a quarterly DSCR test and a customer concentration review at every renewal.

scenarios.label: Revenue drops 20%
scenarios.recommendation: Approve only with material additional conditions
scenarios.memoOverride: Approve only with: 12-month deposit covenant, additional collateral, owner liquidity covenant of $100K minimum, and quarterly DSCR test. Borderline acceptance.
scenarios.avatarScript: DSCR drops to 1.10x — just above the SBA floor. I'd want a deposit covenant, additional collateral, and an owner liquidity covenant before approving. This is borderline.

why_approve.script: Three reasons. Cash flow is more than double the bank floor at 2.84x DSCR. The owner has real skin in the game — $890K net worth and a personal guarantee. And the SBA guaranty covers 75% of our exposure. Risk-adjusted, this is a clean yes.
why_approve.answer: Three reasons: (1) DSCR of 2.84x is more than double the 1.25x bank floor. (2) Owner has $890K net worth with personal guarantee. (3) SBA covers 75% of our exposure. Risk-adjusted, this is a clean approval.

what_worries.script: Honestly, the tariff exposure. 62% of inventory is imported small engines. If tariffs double, margins compress fast. I want a quarterly inventory mix review as a covenant — so we see it coming before it hits the P&L.
what_worries.answer: Primary concern: tariff exposure on 62% imported inventory (small engines). Secondary: customer concentration at 31% for top 3 accounts. Both are manageable but warrant monitoring covenants.

chair.script: If I'm the credit committee chair, I push on two things: document the customer concentration mitigant in writing — not just in the narrative — get it signed by all three customers. And I want a second appraisal on the Fredericksburg property before closing. Otherwise, I'd vote yes.
chair.answer: Two asks before signing: (1) Written documentation of customer concentration mitigants — signed contracts from all three. (2) Second appraisal on Fredericksburg property. With those, vote yes.

conditions: Life insurance assignment per bank policy
Second appraisal on Fredericksburg property pre-closing
